results.question: What is the percentage of parolees who have reoffended in Texas, broken down by gender and race, for the years 2017 and 2018?

    gender,
    race,
    year,
    CAST(SUM(reoffender) AS REAL) * 100 / COUNT(*) AS reoffend_percentage

GROUP BY 
    gender, race, year;

FROM parolee

results.question: What is the change in housing affordability in Portland from Q1 2021 to Q2 2021?

FROM

JOIN 
    portland_housing q2
ON

WHERE 
    q1.quarter = 1 AND q1.year = 2021 AND
    q2.quarter = 2 AND q2.year = 2021;

results.question: Find the average travel time (in days) for vessels traveling between the Port of Valparaiso and the Port of Singapore in the first half of 2021, ranked by the average travel time in ascending order.
results.gold_sql: SELECT route, AVG(travel_time) as avg_travel_time FROM VesselTravel WHERE route = 7 AND departure_date >= '2021-01-01' AND departure_date < '2021-07-01' GROUP BY route ORDER BY avg_travel_time ASC;
results.baseline_sql:
SELECT v.vessel_id, AVG(v.travel_time) AS avg_travel_time
FROM VesselTravel v
JOIN Routes r ON v.route = r.route_id
WHERE r.departure_port = 'Valparaiso' AND r.arrival_port = 'Singapore' 
  AND v.departure_date BETWEEN '2021-01-01' AND '2021-06-30'
GROUP BY v.vessel_id
ORDER BY avg_travel_time ASC;
results.pipeline_sql: SELECT AVG(travel_time) as avg_travel_time FROM VesselTravel AS vt JOIN Routes AS r ON vt.route = r.route_id WHERE r.departure_port = 'Valparaiso' AND r.arrival_port = 'Singapore' AND departure_date BETWEEN '2021-01-01' AND '2021-06-30' GROUP BY vessel_id ORDER BY avg_travel_time ASC

results.question: Which mental health conditions were treated most frequently in Canada during 2022?
results.gold_sql: SELECT conditions.condition, COUNT(conditions.condition) AS count FROM conditions JOIN patients ON conditions.patient_id = patients.id JOIN treatments ON patients.id = treatments.patient_id WHERE patients.country = 'Canada' AND treatments.treatment_date >= '2022-01-01' AND treatments.treatment_date < '2023-01-01' GROUP BY conditions.condition ORDER BY count DESC LIMIT 1;
results.baseline_sql:
SELECT 
    c.condition,
    COUNT(*) AS treatment_count
FROM 
    patients p
JOIN 
    treatments t ON p.id = t.patient_id
JOIN 
    conditions c ON p.id = c.patient_id
WHERE 
    p.country = 'Canada' AND
    YEAR(t.treatment_date) = 2022
GROUP BY

results.question: What is the minimum temperature increase in Europe in any year since 2000, and what is the year in which it occurred?

       year
FROM temperature_data
WHERE region = 'Europe' AND year > 2000;

    COUNT(*) AS count
FROM hospitals
UNION ALL

    COUNT(*) AS count
FROM clinics
UNION ALL

    COUNT(*) AS count
FROM long_term_care;

FROM hospitals 
UNION ALL 
SELECT clinics.type AS facility_type, COUNT(*) AS number_of_facilities 
FROM clinics 
UNION ALL

FROM long_term_care;

results.question: Calculate the moving average of chemical waste production for each facility, for the last 6 months.

        waste_amount,
        AVG(waste_amount) OVER (PARTITION BY facility_id ORDER BY date ROWS BETWEEN 5 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS moving_avg
    FROM 
        facility_waste
)

    facility_id,
    date,
    waste_amount,
    moving_avg
FROM 
    monthly_waste
ORDER BY 
    facility_id, date;

    facility_id, 
    date, 
    waste_amount,

WHERE

results.question: Who has the highest number of wins as a coach for each team in a season?
results.gold_sql: SELECT c.TeamID, c.CoachName, COUNT(CASE WHEN h.HomeTeamResult = 'Win' THEN 1 END) + COUNT(CASE WHEN a.HomeTeamResult = 'Win' THEN 1 END) AS Wins FROM Coach c LEFT JOIN Match h ON c.TeamID = h.HomeTeamID AND h.HomeTeamResult = 'Win' LEFT JOIN Match a ON c.TeamID = a.AwayTeamID AND a.HomeTeamResult = 'Win' GROUP BY c.TeamID, c.CoachName ORDER BY Wins DESC;
results.baseline_sql:
WITH MatchResults AS (
    SELECT 
        HomeTeamID AS TeamID, 
        HomeTeamResult AS Result
    FROM 
        Match
    WHERE 
        HomeTeamResult = 'Win'
    UNION ALL
    SELECT 
        AwayTeamID AS TeamID, 
        CASE 
            WHEN HomeTeamResult = 'Loss' THEN 'Win'
            ELSE 'Loss'
        END AS Result
    FROM 
        Match
    WHERE 
        AwayTeamResult = 'Win'
),
CoachWins AS (
    SELECT 
        c.CoachName, 
        c.TeamID, 
        COUNT(m.Result) AS WinCount
    FROM 
        Coach c
    JOIN 
        MatchResults m ON c.TeamID = m.TeamID AND m.Result = 'Win'
    GROUP BY 
        c.CoachID, c.CoachName, c.TeamID
)
SELECT 
    CoachName, 
    TeamID, 
    MAX(WinCount) AS MaxWins
FROM 
    CoachWins
GROUP BY 
    CoachName, TeamID;
results.pipeline_sql:
SELECT t1.coachname, t3.teamname, COUNT(t2.matchid) AS win_count 
FROM coach AS t1 
JOIN match AS t2 ON t1.teamid = t2.hometeamid 
JOIN team AS t3 ON t1.teamid = t3.teamid 
WHERE t2.homeTeamResult = 'Win' 
GROUP BY t1.coachname, t3.teamname 
ORDER BY win_count DESC

results.question: Which team has the highest number of wins in the 'basketball_games' table?
results.gold_sql: SELECT name AS team, MAX(home_team_wins + away_team_wins) AS highest_wins FROM (SELECT name, CASE WHEN home_team = team_id AND home_team_score > away_team_score THEN 1 ELSE 0 END + CASE WHEN away_team = team_id AND away_team_score > home_team_score THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS home_team_wins, CASE WHEN home_team = team_id AND home_team_score < away_team_score THEN 1 ELSE 0 END + CASE WHEN away_team = team_id AND away_team_score < home_team_score THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS away_team_wins FROM basketball_teams JOIN basketball_games ON basketball_teams.team_id = basketball_games.home_team OR basketball_teams.team_id = basketball_games.away_team) AS subquery GROUP BY name;
results.baseline_sql:
SELECT t.name AS winning_team
FROM basketball_teams t
JOIN basketball_games g ON (t.team_id = g.home_team AND g.home_team_score > g.away_team_score) OR (t.team_id = g.away_team AND g.away_team_score > g.home_team_score)
GROUP BY t.team_id, t.name
ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC
LIMIT 1;
results.pipeline_sql:
SELECT t1.name, SUM(CASE WHEN t2.home_team_score > t2.away_team_score THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) as total_wins 
FROM basketball_teams AS t1 
JOIN basketball_games AS t2 ON t1.team_id = t2.home_team 
GROUP BY t1.team_id 
ORDER BY total_wins DESC 
LIMIT 1

results.question: What is the difference in the average duration of closed cases between attorneys in the "criminal_defense" department, ordered by the difference?

       AVG(c.duration) AS avg_duration,
       (AVG(CASE WHEN c.status = 'closed' THEN c.duration ELSE 0 END) -

FROM attorneys a
JOIN cases c ON a.attorney_id = c.attorney_id
WHERE a.department = 'criminal_defense'
GROUP BY a.name
ORDER BY diff_avg_duration;

results.question: List the ports and their average cargo weight for company "HarborLink" in Q2 2017 and Q3 2017.
results.gold_sql: SELECT port.name, AVG(cargo.weight) FROM port INNER JOIN cargo ON port.id = cargo.port_id AND cargo.quarter IN (2, 3) INNER JOIN company ON cargo.company_id = company.id WHERE company.name = 'HarborLink' GROUP BY port.name;

    p.name AS port_name,
    AVG(c.weight) AS average_weight_q2_2017,
    AVG(CASE WHEN c.quarter = 3 THEN c.weight ELSE NULL END) AS average_weight_q3_2017
FROM 
    cargo c
JOIN 
    company co ON c.company_id = co.id
JOIN 
    port p ON c.port_id = p.id
WHERE 
    co.name = 'HarborLink'
GROUP BY 
    p.name;
results.pipeline_sql:
SELECT port.name, AVG(cargo.weight) AS avg_weight 
FROM port 
INNER JOIN cargo ON port.id = cargo.port_id 
INNER JOIN company ON cargo.company_id = company.id 
WHERE company.name = 'HarborLink' AND (cargo.quarter = 2 OR cargo.quarter = 3) AND year = 2017 
GROUP BY port.name;

results.question: What is the number of traffic accidents in Toronto involving cyclists in the last 3 years, and how many resulted in injuries?

FROM

results.question: Calculate the year-over-year revenue growth for each restaurant.
results.gold_sql: SELECT restaurant_name, (revenue - LAG(revenue) OVER (PARTITION BY restaurant_name ORDER BY year)) / ABS(LAG(revenue) OVER (PARTITION BY restaurant_name ORDER BY year)) as revenue_growth FROM restaurants;
results.baseline_sql:
SELECT r1.restaurant_id, 
       r1.restaurant_name, 
       r1.year AS year_1, 
       r1.revenue AS revenue_1,
       r2.year AS year_2,
       r2.revenue AS revenue_2,
       ((r2.revenue - r1.revenue) / r1.revenue) * 100 AS yoy_growth_percentage
FROM restaurants r1
JOIN restaurants r2 ON r1.restaurant_id = r2.restaurant_id AND r1.year + 1 = r2.year;
results.pipeline_sql:
SELECT restaurant_name, 
       (revenue - LAG(revenue) OVER (PARTITION BY restaurant_id ORDER BY year)) / LAG(revenue) OVER (PARTITION BY restaurant_id ORDER BY year) * 100 AS revenue_growth_percentage 
FROM restaurants 
ORDER BY restaurant_id, year;

results.question: What is the maximum consecutive number of days with a financial wellbeing score below 60 for each customer?
results.gold_sql: SELECT customer_id, MAX(consecutive_below_60) FROM (SELECT customer_id, score_date, financial_wellbeing_score, COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE financial_wellbeing_score < 60) OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY score_date ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND 1 PRECEDING) AS consecutive_below_60 FROM customer_scores) subquery GROUP BY customer_id;
results.baseline_sql:
WITH ConsecutiveDays AS (
    SELECT
        customer_id,
        score_date,
        financial_wellbeing_score,
        CASE 
            WHEN financial_wellbeing_score < 60 THEN 1 ELSE NULL 
        END AS flag,
        SUM(CASE 
                WHEN financial_wellbeing_score < 60 THEN 1 ELSE 0 
            END) OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY score_date ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS grp
    FROM customer_scores
),
ConsecutiveCounts AS (
    SELECT
        customer_id,
        COUNT(*) AS consecutive_count
    FROM ConsecutiveDays
    WHERE flag = 1
    GROUP BY customer_id, grp
)
SELECT
    customer_id,
    MAX(consecutive_count) AS max_consecutive_days_below_60
FROM ConsecutiveCounts
GROUP BY customer_id;
results.pipeline_sql:
SELECT customer_id, MAX(consecutive_days) as max_consecutive_below_60 
FROM (
    SELECT customer_id, 
           CASE WHEN financial_wellbeing_score < 60 THEN consecutive_days + 1 ELSE 0 END AS consecutive_days
    FROM (
        SELECT customer_id, 
               financial_wellbeing_score,
               SUM(CASE WHEN financial_wellbeing_score >= 60 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY score_date ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) as consecutive_days
        FROM customer_scores
    )
)
WHERE consecutive_days > 0
GROUP BY customer_id;
